summary: Tested phone sign-up/sign-in (Telesign, simulated +1555 numbers) and auto-renew for eSIM / USA mobile numbers, on both backend and frontend. Backend: 12/12 pytest pass, plus a probe that sends 40 wrong codes at once (MAX_TRIES=5 held), and esim_renewal.test.js prints PASS. Frontend: signup on the phone tab -> code step with preview code -> wrong code shows 'Wrong code. Try again.' -> right code lands on /cloudivr/app; settings-phone shows +1555..., settings-email is absent; the top bar shows 'Signed in as +1555...' at 1920px. Login with the same number (typed as '+1 (555) 479-3807') reached the same account id (5000000000000019). The 30s countdown ran 30->25s; after it ended, call-me and text-again buttons appeared; voice gave a new code and showed 'We're calling ...'. The email tab is the default and Alice's email login works. Auto-renew switches (esim-buy-autorenew, mobile-offer-autorenew, esim-co-autorenew, mobile-co-autorenew) are role=switch, aria-checked=true by default, and flip on click. Intercepted POST bodies: /esim autoRenew:false, /mobile-numbers autoRenew:true then false. Manage cards show 'renews YYYY-MM-DD' or 'Auto-renew off · ends YYYY-MM-DD', and the toggles flip both ways. No critical bugs; only minor issues below.

minor.issue: The per-IP budget is 10 codes / 15 min (recordFailure(ipKey,10)) and every request counts, even successful ones. Users behind a shared NAT (offices, mobile carrier CGNAT) could hit 429 too_many_codes quickly. Consider a higher IP limit.

The tries check (c.tries >= MAX_TRIES) runs before $inc and is not atomic. 40 parallel guesses through the ingress counted only 5 (held in the test), but an atomic findOneAndUpdate({tries:{$lt:5}},{$inc}) would close it fully.

ui_bugs.issue: autoRenew is useState(true) and ignores draft.autoRenew. A landing-page eSIM buyer who turned auto-renew OFF, paid by crypto and later finished the order in the app (draft resume) gets auto-renew ON.

ui_bugs.component: Landing checkout Account step (EsimCheckout.Account, reused by MobileCheckout)
ui_bugs.issue: Only email/password sign-up is offered; there is no phone sign-up option, though phone onboarding is a requested feature.

issues: Different price formats: eSIM shows '$75/month · renews …' but mobile shows '$75.00/month · renews …'
The mobile toggle (mobile-autorenew-{id}) is a plain text button with no switch graphic, while the eSIM toggle has one
'Forgot password?' link still shows on the phone tab, where it does not apply
OFF track is rgb(226,232,240) with a white knob: very low contrast. The ~150ms transition also makes screenshots taken right after a click look still ON

action_items: Esim.js BuyForm: start autoRenew from draft?.autoRenew !== false so the landing-checkout choice survives the draft resume
Optional: offer phone sign-up in the landing checkout Account step
Optional: make the tries increment atomic in /auth/phone/verify; review the per-IP limit of 10 codes / 15 min
Minor UI polish: one price format on manage cards, a switch graphic on the mobile toggle, hide 'Forgot password?' on the phone tab, more contrast for the OFF switch in the light theme
critical_code_review_comments: phone-auth.js is clean: E.164 normalization, codes stored as hashes, 5-minute TTL index, one-time use via findOneAndUpdate({used:false}), partial unique index on phone, E11000 race handled on account creation
2FA email setup already guards phone-only accounts (no_email); emails.send skips accounts with no email
spenza.js renewal: billOne/expire/setAutoRenew logic matches the spec; renew() turns autoRenew back on after a manual payment (intended)
seed_data_creation: Phone test accounts +15554793807 (id 5000000000000019) plus several random +1555 accounts from pytest (names TEST_*). Alice bought one mobile line mn_272f87444e91 (autoRenew false) through the API, then it was cancelled. Alice's wallet went down $75 (now ~$399.79). The test clears webLoginAttempts keys 'phone-send|<ip>' between runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The phone code limit is 10 per IP per 15 min. Clear it with mongosh test: db.webLoginAttempts.deleteMany({_id:/^phone-send\|\d/}). The pytest does this automatically. Intercept POST /esim and /mobile-numbers with page.route to avoid spending Alice's wallet. The esim page is /cloudivr/app/esim (it lists both eSIM and mobile lines); the mobile offer is at /cloudivr/app/buy (mobile-offer-start, then mobile-offer-pay-button); the in-app eSIM pay button is esim-pay-button.
